question.text: Identify the Incan ruler whom Pizarro seized and executed after demanding and receiving a roomful of gold as ransom.
question.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

swap.text: The Incan empire was centered in this modern day country, whose capital is Lima.
swap.clue: A culture in this country built the site of Cahuachi.

question.text: This Incan "lost city" is believed to have been built for Pachacuti. It was re-discovered in 1911 by Hiram Bingham.
question.clue: It is believed that it served as a retreat for Pachacuti Yupanqui, who had conquered the region of Tampu.

swap.leadin: Name some things about pre-Columbian Peru.
swap.text: This southern Peruvian civilization created an aqueduct system that still works. It drew lines in spider, fish, and lizard shapes in a namesake desert, and also shares its name with a tectonic plate that borders the Andes.
swap.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

question.leadin: This country fought the Cenepa and Paquisha Wars against its northern neighbor, Ecuador.
question.text: Name this country, home to the cities of Arequipa and its capital, Lima.
question.clue: A culture from this country based in Sipan was known for pottery depicting exaggerated sexual acts, and another civilization in this country was known for geoglyphs depicting Condors and Herons.

swap.text: The Incas lived in this mountain range, in which they developed a series of bridges and roads to improve communication.
swap.clue: A culture in this mountain range depicted a spider called the "Decapitator" and created a mummy known as the Lord of Sipan.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Andean civilizations.
question.text: This culture existed in the Ica river valley succeeding the Paracas culture. These people are famous for theirnamesake lines which form geoglyphs visible from the sky.

swap.leadin: Name the following regarding the Wiphala [wi-PAH-lah].
swap.text: Andeans speak this indigenous language, which also names them. It is a primary language group, also called Runa Simi.
swap.clue: The MUPP-NP party's common name is a word in this language that's gained popularity with indigenists for its connotation of "world reversal."

question.leadin: A first-year undergrad named Manny Medrano helped decode a system used in these things.
question.text: Identify these records made from alpaca and llama fibers, most commonly used for keeping track of tribute.
question.clue: The coarsest wool was instead woven by commoners and used to make chusi, a cloth used for ch'uspa sacks and blankets, or the knotted cords that comprise these recordkeeping devices.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
swap.text: One of the leaders of this confederation ritually covered himself in gold dust before diving into Lake Guatavita. This confederation, which was led by a Zipa and a Zaque ["ZAH-kay"], held territory in the highlands of modern-day Colombia.
swap.clue: Perhaps this polity's most well-known artefact is known as this polity's "raft", which is a gold sculpture that was found in Lake Guatavita.

question.leadin: Early colonial writer Juan Freyle wrote an account of a ceremony in which a new ruler of these people was covered in gold dust and submerged in Lake Guatavita.
question.text: Name this confederation of Northern Andean tribes that was led by co-rulers called Zipa and Zaque. They were encountered by the Conquistador Gonzalo Jimenez de Quesada after his expedition sailed up the Magdalena.
question.clue: This people, who mined salt in large gacha pots and imported gold for tunjo figures of humans or animals at Guatavita.

swap.leadin: The Aschers did work uncoding the number system used on these devices, where zero is represented by a missing knot.
swap.text: Name these devices. Made from knotted string, these devices were extensively used in the administration of the Inca prior to their invasion by Francisco Pizarro.
swap.clue: This devices that were made of string and were commonly used for keeping census records or for monitoring taxes. The information on these devices was stored using knots.

question.leadin: Construction with this quality, visible at the Acllahuasi at Cuzco, necessitated masons to precisely shape stones to fit with other pieces on site.
question.text: Name or describe this limitation of the rubble masonry in Incan walls. The term "drystone" refers to masonry made with this limitation.
question.answerHtml: built without mortar [accept answer involving no fill or material between stones]

swap.leadin: The former MIT student Lori Berenson was accused of collaborating with a modern organization named for this person.
swap.text: Identify this man who names a "Revolutionary Movement" led by Victor Campos. This Indigenous rebel, who took his name from a monarch executed at Vilcabamba, was defeated at the 1780 Battle of Sangarara.
swap.answerHtml: Túpac Amaru II [in place of “Túpac” accept Thupaq or Thupa or Topa; in place of “Amaru” accept Amaro; accept Túpac Amaru Revolutionary Movement; prompt on José Gabriel Condorcanqui by asking “what name did he adopt?”; prompt on MRTA]
swap.clue: This leader's revolt targeted the expansion of the alcabala and a system of forced mining labour called the mit'a.

question.leadin: This city was the location of a "Ransom Room" full of gold offered by a ruler to his captor.
question.text: Name this city. A battle named for this city allegedly began after that aforementioned ruler threw down a Bible presented to him by Vincente de Valverde.
question.answerHtml: Cajamarca (“ka-ha-MAR-ka”) [or Kashamarka; accept Battle of Cajamarca; accept Massacre at Cajamarca]
question.clue: The mixed-race Juan Garcia held a post as town crier in this Peruvian city after participating in Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire, during which Atahualpa was captured in this city led by a lord who collaborated with the Spanish.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about follicularly challenged beings from history.
swap.text: Hairless orchid dogs named after this empire were one of the six dog breeds recorded by its colonizers. Figure-eight knots made of hair were used to transmit messages across this empire.
swap.answerHtml: Incan Empire [accept Peruvian Incan hairless dog; accept Peruvian Inca Orchid]
swap.clue: Quizquiz ("kees-kees") served as a general of this empire under Huayna Capac and helped another ruler of this empire win a civil war against his brother Huascar.

question.leadin: Answer the following about archaeological discoveries that involve ancient astronauts.
question.text: Von Daniken also said that ancient astronauts used these features as landing-strips for spaceships. These ancient geoglyphs were created by an eponymous Peruvian culture.
question.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about exhumed corpses across world history.
swap.text: This man's corpse was exhumed in 1892 to show in a glass coffin, but it was found in 1977 to be the wrong body. Forces loyal to "El Mozo" killed this man after his brothers captured El Mozo's father in battle at Las Salinas.
swap.clue: He led a band dubbed the "Famous 13" and gained over twenty tons of precious metals after setting up the "Ransom Room."

question.leadin: One attacking division in this battle was led by a young Hernando de Soto.
question.text: Name this 1532 battle where Francisco Pizarro ambushed and captured the Incan emperor Atahualpa.
question.clue: The losing side in this battle was engaged in a civil war against Huascar and was crippled by the decision to leave the bulk of its army outside the city walls.

swap.leadin: This ruler exempted Quechua speakers from taxation.
swap.text: Name this son of Viracocha who defeated the Chanca invasion of Cuzco. The sun temple Coricancha, and possibly Machu Picchu, were built by this ruler.
swap.clue: This ruler, who legendarily subjugated the (+) Chanka people with stone warriors, organized his realm into four suyus.
